newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Europe well supplied with cocoa, prices slack.
newsitem.headline: Europe well supplied with cocoa, prices slack.

text.p: Ample shipments of cocoa to Western Europe are keeping the physical market well supplied and differentials under pressure while currency factors continue to limit offtake, traders said on Wednesday.
Shippers in Ivory Coast were reported to be offering cocoa for March and April delivery, but industry offtake was low despite forecasts of the market moving into deficit this season.
"There is enough cocoa around, and that's the end of the story," one trader said. "The chocolate industry sees this and won't hear any talk of deficits."
Brokers GNI said on Tuesday that world cocoa supply could post a deficit of 180,000 tonnes in the 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) season compared with an estimated surplus of 161,000 in 1995/96.
It said the supply gap could lead to second-month futures rallying to 1,050 or even 1,600 stg a tonne in the coming months.
"Clearly the market is ripe for a major price move," it said, adding the caveat that the margin for error would remain high until the end of January, when a clearer picture of arrivals would emerge.
London cocoa futures were languishing around 880 stg, basis March, on Wednesday with the market seemingly stuck in a protracted downtrend.
Although the terminal market has moved sharply lower in the past months, sterling's strength has meant many potential buyers in Europe have not seen any benefit.
"For those holding marks or guilders, they are paying the same price they were a few months ago," another trader said.
Trade sources estimated that cover held by chocolate manufacturers remained steady at between eight and nine months and their buying patterns.
"It's hand-to-mouth buying and nothing more," one said.

Cocoa shipments were continuing to arrive in Amsterdam and other ports of northwest Europe. The latest figures from warehousing firm SGS showed Amsterdam stocks at 468,000 tonnes at the end of December, up 53,000 from a month earlier. Traders estimated that the current figure approached 500,000 tonnes.
Bulk shipments have formed part of the total. Major grinders are each planning to ship in one or two cargoes a month over the coming season, each shipment comprising 4,000 to 6,000 tonnes.
"The bulk shipments have started and are progressing well. There are no major problems with them," an industry source said.
German cocoa traders, lamenting a lacklustre physical market, said they were hoping for a demand boost from the international annual confectionery fair ISM in Cologne from January 26 to 30.
